name: Calendly
whatYouLose: Round-robin and collective team scheduling out of the box
Native Zoom/Teams link creation without wiring OAuth yourself
The recognizable "pick a time" link people already trust
Polished mobile apps and calendar sync edge cases (time zones, DST, recurring holds)
prompt:
Build a self-hosted scheduling page, a Calendly replacement for one person.

Stack: Node + Hono, SQLite, server-rendered HTML, no client framework.
Features:
- Public page /:eventSlug with a month calendar and available time slots in the visitor's time zone.
- Availability rules: weekly hours, buffer before/after, minimum notice, max bookings per day.
- Read busy times from my Google Calendar (OAuth, freebusy API) and write confirmed events back with a Google Meet link.
- Booking form (name, email, notes) → confirmation page + .ics attachment emailed via SMTP to both parties.
- Cancel/reschedule links with signed tokens.
- Admin page behind a single password env var to edit event types.
Done when: npm run dev serves a working booking flow, and tests cover slot generation across a DST change.
notes: Single-user scheduling is a solved, well-documented problem: slot math plus the Google Calendar freebusy API. The hard parts are teams and calendar edge cases, which a solo user rarely hits.
